ARKFLAME STUDIOS / BROWSER TOOLS

GLOBAL DOM OPTIMIZER VERSION 0.0.6

A cleaner,
faster web.

Long conversations, articles, feeds and documentation should stay responsive. Global DOM Optimizer helps Chromium skip unnecessary rendering of eligible content outside the viewport—without removing it from the page.

Download v0.0.6 ZIP How it works ↗

For Chromium and Helium · Manual installation (unpacked) · Chrome Web Store listing pending

✓ Automatic containment ✓ On-device processing ✓ Per-site control

HOW IT WORKS

Less work beyond what you see.

Content remains in the document. Supported sections far from view can skip layout and painting until you approach them.

01

Detect independent blocks

Identifies eligible paragraphs, messages, articles, code and image sections—even inside nested scrollers.

02

Skip offscreen rendering

Uses native content-visibility containment rather than deleting nodes or rewriting the website.

03

Restore content on approach

Viewport-aware observation and cached scan regions bring nearby elements back as you scroll.

BUILT FOR REAL PAGES

Quietly useful. Fully in control.

▤

Long-form content

Designed for lengthy AI conversations, documents, tutorials and image-rich feeds.

▦

Incremental scanning

Tracks structural changes in cached regions instead of rescanning the entire page after each update.

◎

Live diagnostics

Inspect managed blocks, offscreen coverage estimates, scan counts and local scan work.

◇

Your choice per website

One automatic optimization strategy, plus a global switch and a site-specific on/off control.

GET STARTED

Install in under a minute.

Download the extension, unzip it, then open chrome://extensions in your Chromium-based browser. Enable Developer mode and select Load unpacked.

Download the extension ZIP ↓

Designed to be safe, not magical.

Optimization varies by site and device. Interactive elements may be left untouched, and reduced rendering work does not guarantee a particular FPS, CPU or RAM improvement. The percentage in the extension is an estimated scroll-height coverage metric—not a benchmark result.
